f1.quote: The study compared the oxidation behavior of the as-printed alloy with material aged at 750°C for 50 h.

f2.quote: Aging produced approximately 25–30 vol% homogeneously distributed Ni/Ti-enriched L12 nanoscale precipitates

f3.quote: larger Al/Ti-enriched, Cr/Fe-depleted L21 precipitates, mainly near cell walls.

f4.quote: Polished 7.5 × 7.5 × 3 mm samples were oxidized for up to 96 h at 600, 750, 900, 1050, and 1200°C.

f6.quote: A duplex-to-trilayer oxide scale developed: an outer layer containing elemental and mixed/spinel oxides, a continuous homogeneous Cr-rich oxide (primarily Cr2O3) layer, and an inner discontinuous Al/Ti-rich oxide region.

f7.quote: preferential outward Cr diffusion formed a dense Cr2O3 barrier that restricted inward oxygen and outward metal-ion diffusion

f8.quote: Cr-depleted precipitates and additional matrix–precipitate interfaces delayed formation of an equally protective Cr-oxide scale

f9.quote: additional matrix–precipitate interfaces delayed formation of an equally protective Cr-oxide scale and provided possible short-circuit oxygen-diffusion paths.

f10.quote: Relative to the as-printed baseline, precipitation-aged material was expected to show higher oxidation mass gain, particularly as temperature increased

f11.quote: Mass-gain kinetics were mainly subparabolic at 750–900°C, although behavior at 600°C was near parabolic and the aged alloy returned to near-parabolic behavior at 900°C.

f12.quote: both states were expected to retain broadly similar high-temperature oxide-growth activation energies
